english_scripts:
uḍuttu kkaḻainda nin pīdagavāḍai uḍuttu
kalattaduṇḍu
toḍutta tuzāymalar śūḍi kkaḻaindana
śūḍumittoṇḍargaḻōm
viḍutta tiśai kkarumam tirutti
tiruvōṇa ttiruvizavil
paḍutta painnāgaṇai ppaḻḻikoṇḍānukku
pallāṇḍu kūṟudumē
meaning: We, Your servants, wear the garments once worn by You. We partake of the sacred remnants offered to You and adorn ourselves with garlands and Tulasi that once graced Your divine form. We long to serve You eternally, both here and in the supreme abode, seeking everlasting service at Your feet.
purport:
Now, together with all the gathered devotees, Periyāḻvār sings auspicious benedictions for Bhagavān. In this pāsuram, the Āḻvār expresses that he desires only those things that have already been used and enjoyed by Bhagavān, never anything fresh or independent of Him. He declares that he wishes to wear only the *Pītāmbara* worn by the Lord. Here, the Āḻvār refers to the Lord's divine garment not merely as cloth, but as a sacred servant of Bhagavān. Just as Sudarśana is the foremost among the Lord's weapons and Garuḍa among His vehicles, *Pītāmbara* is revered as a *Nitya-sūri* who serves the Lord in the form of His divine garment.

Periyavāccān Piḷḷai explains that devotees cherish garments that bear the remnants of Bhagavān's sandal paste and turmeric, for such garments have already adorned His divine form. The devotee desires no ornament, fragrance, or adornment apart from that which has first been associated with Bhagavān.

Likewise, the Āḻvār proclaims that the devotees partake only of food that has first been offered to the Lord. Indeed, Śrī Kṛṣṇa teaches that all food should be offered to Him before being consumed, for everything that sustains life is ultimately granted through His grace. Offering food to Bhagavān is therefore an expression of gratitude and acknowledgment of His supreme ownership. The devotees do not consider anything their own; they receive everything back as His *prasāda*.

The Āḻvār further declares that they would gladly wear the garlands adorning Bhagavān. This sentiment evokes the divine episode of Āṇḍāḷ, who lovingly wore the garlands before offering them to the Lord. Those very garlands, sanctified by both the devotion of Āṇḍāḷ and the acceptance of Bhagavān, become objects of immense reverence. The devotees desire to wear only such garlands, for they have already been enjoyed by those whom they cherish the most.

Periyāḻvār then describes the spirit in which devotees serve Bhagavān. Their service is not mechanical or merely dutiful. It is rendered with utmost care, affection, and attentiveness. Just as Hanumān, when sent as a messenger to Sītā Devī, accomplished far more than the task assigned to him by assessing the strength of Rāvaṇa, understanding the condition of Laṅkā, and demonstrating the power of Śrī Rāma to the enemy, true devotees always seek to perform whatever pleases Bhagavān the most. Their sole concern is His delight and welfare.

Thus, the gathered devotees join Periyāḻvār in singing the Lord's glories. They praise the Lord of *Śravaṇa* Nakṣatra. They behold His divine form resting upon the pure white coils of Ādiśeṣa. Against that radiant white background, His dark cloud-hued form shines with incomparable beauty, resembling a rain-laden cloud resting upon a snow-white mountain peak.

Captivated by this vision, they sing in loving concern and *vātsalya-bhāva*: “O Lord who reclines upon the spotless white Ādiśeṣa! O dark cloud-hued One of immeasurable beauty! May You live long for countless ages and eons. May Your glory ever flourish. May You remain eternally auspicious!”

tamil_scripts: எந்நாள் எம்பெருமான்உன்தனக்கடியோம் என்றெழுத்துப்பட்ட அந்நாளேஅடியோங்கள் அடிக்குடில்வீடு பெற்றுய்ந்தது காண்செந்நாள் தோற்றித்திருமதுரையுள் சிலைகுனித்துஐந்தலைய பைந்நாகத் தலை பாய்ந்தவனே !உன்னைப் பல்லாண்டு கூறுதுமே
english_scripts:
ennāḻ emberumān
undanakkaḍiyōm enṟezuttuppaṭṭa annāḻē
aḍiyōṅgaḻ aḍikkuḍil
vīḍu peṭruyndadu kāṇ
śennāḻ tōṭri
tirumaduraiyuḻ śilaikunittu
aindalaiya painnāga ttalai pāyndavanē !
unnai ppallāṇḍu kūṟudumē
meaning: Service rendered purely out of love, without expectation of reward, is the highest joy. On the day we surrendered ourselves as Your eternal servants, Your grace uplifted even our humble lineage. Let us therefore sing Pallāṇḍu in praise of You, O Lord who was born in Mathurā, shattered the mighty bow of Kaṁsa, and subdued the serpent Kāliya through Your divine play.
purport:
The *Bhāgavatas* continue to sing the glories of the Lord alongside Periyāḻvār. Among them, the former *Kaivalyārthis* now proclaim with great joy: “We have realized that serving You alone grants the highest bliss, a joy that can never be attained either through mere *ātmānubhava* or through the pursuit of fleeting worldly pleasures.” Having experienced the grace of Bhagavān, they now understand that the delight of *bhagavad-kainkarya* surpasses every other attainment.

They declare that the day they surrendered at the lotus feet of Bhagavān through the grace of an Ācārya was the day they were truly reborn. It was a birth that would never lead to another birth. On that auspicious day, they beheld the beauty of the Lord, were uplifted from the sufferings of *saṁsāra*, and obtained the assurance of His protection. They further proclaim that the grace they received extended not merely to themselves, but to their entire lineage.

Just as Śrī Rāma granted refuge not only to Vibhīṣaṇa but also to all those who accompanied him, though Vibhīṣaṇa alone formally sought surrender, Bhagavān extends His protection to all who are associated with His devotees. Such is the greatness of His compassion. Therefore, the devotees declare that the day one receives the grace of an Ācārya and is blessed with the sacred *Aṣṭākṣara Mahāmantra* is the day the *jīvātmā* begins its ascent beyond the cycle of birth and death. “All glories,” they proclaim, “to that Lord who grants the highest and most enduring joy!”

The devotees then sing the protection of the Lord who appeared among humanity as Śrī Kṛṣṇa. They marvel at His boundless compassion, wondering how eyes fashioned from material elements were blessed with the fortune of beholding His divine form, His incomparable beauty, and His wondrous *līlās*. Overwhelmed with gratitude, they exclaim: “O Lord, we have surrendered unto You, who appeared under the auspicious conjunction of Aṣṭamī and Rohiṇī Nakṣatra. O Lord of Jayanthi, we sing Your protection and pray that You may live long for countless ages!”

Their minds then turn to the glorious deeds of Kṛṣṇa. “Did You not dance upon the hoods of the serpent Kāliya and subdue his arrogance? Did You not shatter the pride of Kaṁsa and break the mighty bow in Mathurā? Did You not repeatedly protect the righteous and destroy the forces of evil?” Recalling these divine acts, the devotees are filled with *vātsalya-bhāva* and loving concern for the Lord.

Therefore they conclude their song with affectionate benedictions: “O Kṛṣṇa, protector of all worlds, may You live long! May no harm or misfortune ever approach You! May Your glory ever increase! This alone is our desire. We seek neither worldly pleasures nor liberation itself. Our only wish is to sing Your praises and offer our loving protection for all eternity.”

tamil_scripts: அல்வழக்கொன்றும் இல்லாஅணி கோட்டியர் கோன்அபிமான துங்கன் செல்வனைப்போலத்திருமாலே ! நானும் உனக்குப் பழவடியேன்நல்வகையால் நமோ நாராயணாவென்றுநாமம் பல பரவிபல்வகையாலும் பவித்திரனே !உன்னைப் பல்லாண்டு கூறுவனே
english_scripts:
alvazakkonṟum illā
aṇi kōṭṭiyar kōn
abimāna tuṅgan śelvanaippōla
tirumālē ! nānum unakku ppazavaḍiyēn
nalvagaiyāl namō nārāyaṇāvenṟu
nāmam pala paravi
palvagaiyālum pavittiranē !
unnai ppallāṇḍu kūṟuvanē
meaning: O Tirumāl, Consort of Śrī Lakṣmī, I am now and forever Your devoted servant, just as the noble Selva Nampi was. Pure and free from wickedness, he was renowned for his devotion to You and Your devotees. I too am Your ancient and eternal servant. Let me sing Pallāṇḍu in Your praise and proclaim with all my heart, “Namaḥ Nārāyaṇāya.”
purport:
Finally, the transformed *Aiśvaryārthis* join Periyāḻvār in singing auspicious benedictions for the Lord. They now proclaim that they have become devotees like Selva Nambi. Even among those devoted to Bhagavān, there remains the subtle danger of pride. A devotee may think, “Through my actions, devotion, and service, I have attained Bhagavān or become qualified for liberation.” Such pride, though seemingly spiritual, still obscures the true nature of the *jīvātmā*. The true *prapannas*, however, recognize that everything is attained solely through the grace of Bhagavān. They declare, “It is only by the mercy of Bhagavān that I, a servant of His servants, have been able to attain Him and become eligible for the supreme abode of *Paramapada*.” Selva Nambi was one such devotee who was completely free from even this subtle form of pride.

Selva Nambi, who belonged to the sacred town of Tirukkoṣṭiyūr, a place that shone like a precious jewel among holy kṣetras, was a great *Bhāgavata*. A Pāṇḍya king, troubled by doubts concerning Vedānta and desirous of knowing who the Supreme Brahman truly is, sought the assistance of Selva Nambi. Although Nambi himself knew the answers to the king's questions, he desired that not only the king but the entire royal assembly should benefit from hearing these truths from a great devotee of Bhagavān. Therefore, he advised the king to convene a grand assembly where scholars and devotees could gather and address these profound questions.

It was in this assembly that Periyāḻvār established the supremacy of Nārāyaṇa and expounded the true nature of the *jīvātmā*. Through his words, the court came to understand that Nārāyaṇa alone is the Supreme Brahman and that the *jīvātmā* exists solely for His service. Delighted by Periyāḻvār's wisdom and devotion, the king honored him by seating him upon a royal elephant and leading him in procession. During this glorious occasion, Bhagavān manifested before the Āḻvār, inspiring the outpouring of *Tiruppallāṇḍu*. Thus, Selva Nambi became an instrument through whom this divine event was brought about.

Selva Nambi was renowned for being free from all inauspicious qualities. He was called “Selva,” meaning one who possesses true wealth. Yet his wealth was not material prosperity. His true wealth was *bhagavad-kainkarya*, loving service to Bhagavān. Therefore, the transformed *Aiśvaryārthis* now proclaim, “We too seek that same wealth possessed by Selva Nambi. We no longer desire worldly riches or temporary attainments. Our treasure is service to Bhagavān, and we have come here solely to serve Him.”

They further declare: “We chant the Lord's names in countless ways and glorify Him through innumerable expressions of devotion. We are the servants of Tirumāl. We are the servants of the Divine Couple together, Śrīman Nārāyaṇa united eternally with Śrī Mahālakṣmī. We remain forever under Their service and protection. O Lord, we are Yours alone. We desire to serve You through every possible form of *kainkarya*. Therefore, we sing auspicious benedictions for Your protection. May You live long forever. May Your glory flourish through endless ages and eons!”

tamil_scripts: பல்லாண்டென்று பவித்திரனைப்பரமேட்டியைசார்ங்கம் என்னும் வில்லாண்டான் தன்னைவில்லிபுத்தூர் விட்டுசித்தன் விரும்பிய சொல்நல்லாண்டென்று நவின்றுரைப்பார்நமோ நாராயணாயென்றுபல்லாண்டும் பரமாத்மனைச்சூழ்ந்திருந்தேத்துவர் பல்லாண்டே
english_scripts:
pallāṇḍenṟu pavittiranai\
paramēṭṭiyai\
śārṅgam ennum villāṇḍān tannai\
villiputtūr viṭṭuśittan virumbiya śol\
nallāṇḍenṟu navinṟuraippār\
namō nārāyaṇāyavenṟu\
pallāṇḍum paramātmanai\
śūzndirundēttuvar pallāṇḍē
meaning: This hymn of Pallāṇḍu was composed by Viṣṇucitta of Śrīvilliputtūr in praise of the Supreme Lord who resides in the eternal realm. With heartfelt devotion he sang, “May You remain ever prosperous.” Whoever recites this hymn with devotion and regards it as a blessing bestowed by grace will join in chanting “Namaḥ Nārāyaṇāya.” By His mercy, they shall attain liberation and dwell near Him forever, singing Pallāṇḍu in endless praise.
purport:
Periyāḻvār concludes the *prabandham* by calling upon all devotees to sing auspicious benedictions for the Lord at all times, in all places, and under all circumstances. The *Tiruppallāṇḍu* is unique among hymns, for it is a composition that offers protection to Bhagavān Himself. Filled with boundless *vātsalya-bhāva*, the Āḻvār sees the Supreme Lord and instinctively bursts forth in concern for His welfare, blessing Him with *pallāṇḍu*. Bhagavān is celebrated in the *Viṣṇu Sahasranāma* as *Pavitrāṇāṁ Pavitramyo*. He is the purifier of all that is pure and the auspiciousness behind all that is auspicious. In ordinary experience, when something impure comes into contact with something pure, the pure object itself becomes tainted. Yet Bhagavān is unlike anything in this world. Even when the most inauspicious of beings comes into contact with Him, it is not He who is affected. Rather, the impure itself becomes purified by His association. He is the source of purity, the measure of auspiciousness, and the one who bestows sanctity upon all things. Therefore, He is praised as *Pavitrāṇāṁ Pavitram* and *Maṅgalānāṁ Maṅgalam*.

Periyāḻvār further reflects upon the relationship between Bhagavān and the *jīvātmā*. Ordinarily, the *jīvātmā* governs and directs the body in which it resides. Bhagavān, however, stands in an even higher relationship to all beings. He is not merely the indwelling ruler of the body; He is the *Ātmā* of the *jīvātmā* itself. As the *Antaryāmin*, He controls, sustains, and guides both the *jīvātmā* and the body. Thus, He alone is the true inner ruler of all existence.

This sacred hymn was composed by Viṣṇucitta, whose mind was constantly immersed in the contemplation of the all-pervading Viṣṇu. Those who recite this *Tiruppallāṇḍu* with devotion, understanding their true nature as belonging entirely to Bhagavān, and who meditate upon the essence of the *Aṣṭākṣara Mahāmantra* embodied in the phrase “Namo Nārāyaṇa,” attain the grace of the Lord. Through such remembrance, the *jīvātmā* becomes freed from all inauspiciousness, transcends the cycle of birth and death, and attains the supreme abode of Bhagavān.

Therefore, Periyāḻvār's final message is an invitation to all devotees: “Sing *pallāṇḍu* to our beloved Lord everywhere, at all times, and in every direction. Glorify Him ceaselessly and proclaim His auspiciousness. For when the Lord is praised and protected through loving devotion, even the most inauspicious of times becomes supremely auspicious. Let every place become sanctified by His names, and let every moment be filled with *pallāṇḍu*.”

tamil_scripts: கண்ணி நுண் சிறுத் தாம்பினால்கட்டுண்ணப் பண்ணிய பெருமாயன்என்னப்பனில்நண்ணித் தென் குருகூர்நம்பி என்றக்கால்அண்ணிக்கும் அமுதூறும்என் நாவுக்கே
english_scripts:
kaṇṇi nuṇ śiṟu ttāmbināl
kaṭṭuṇṇa ppaṇṇiya perumāyan
ennappanil
naṇṇi tten kurugūr
nambi enṟakkāl
aṇṇikkum amudūṟum
ennāvukkē
meaning: My Lord, Kaṇṇan Emperumān, the Supreme Being Himself, allowed Himself to be bound by thin little ropes in the hands of Yaśōdā. Yet sweeter than that divine sight, and more nectarean to my tongue, is the very act of chanting the name of Nammāḻvār, the glorious leader of Southern Thirukkuṟugūr. His name lingers on my tongue with bliss greater than any divine pastime of the Lord.
purport:
With exclusive devotion towards Nammāḻvār, his Ācārya, Madhurakavi Āḻvār composed the divine Prabandham *Kaṇṇinuṇ Ciṟuttāmbu*. Throughout this Prabandham, he establishes the principle of *Ācārya Śeṣatvam* to its highest extent. For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Nammāḻvār is everything. His attachment to his Ācārya is so absolute that Nammāḻvār becomes dearer, closer, and more significant to him than even Bhagavān, the Sarvaśeṣi Himself. This is not a diminution of Bhagavān's greatness, but rather an expression of the supreme reverence accorded to the Ācārya, through whom Bhagavān is truly known and attained.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār begins the Prabandham by recalling Śrī Kṛṣṇa's celebrated Dāmodara līlā. Nammāḻvār, upon experiencing this divine event through his spiritual vision, became overwhelmed by the Lord's *Saulabhyam*. The Supreme Being, the ruler and controller of countless universes, allowed Himself to be bound by Yaśodā with a simple rope. The sweetness of this act so captivated Nammāḻvār that he remained immersed in divine ecstasy and unconscious to the external world for months. Therefore, Madhurakavi Āḻvār deliberately chooses this incident as the opening theme of his work.

The rope used by Yaśodā was a short cord tied together with many knots, yet it was insufficient to encircle the Lord. The Supreme Lord, who pervades all existence and transcends all limitations, cannot truly be measured or contained by anything within creation. Yet, out of affection for Yaśodā's boundless motherly love (*vātsalya*), Bhagavān Himself contracted His divine form and allowed Himself to be bound. The rope left marks upon His abdomen, earning Him the name Dāmodara. The Lord who binds the entire universe within His Māyā willingly submitted Himself to being bound by His devotee. The One who liberates all souls from the bondage of saṁsāra accepted bondage for the sake of love. What an astonishing mystery! What immeasurable compassion, accessibility, and affection shine forth in this divine pastime!

Yet Madhurakavi Āḻvār declares that his master Nammāḻvār, who experienced and revealed these divine truths, is even sweeter and more accessible to him than Bhagavān Himself. There was once a time when his heart was drawn directly towards Bhagavān. Now, however, he has surrendered completely to the sacred feet of Nammāḻvār, the exalted saint of Tirukkurugūr, lovingly known as *Teṉkurugūr Nambi*. Nammāḻvār is the very embodiment of *Kṛṣṇa-tṛṣṇā-bhakti*, an insatiable thirst for Kṛṣṇa and His divine qualities.

Such is Madhurakavi Āḻvār's devotion that merely uttering the name of his Ācārya fills him with indescribable joy. Every time he recites the name of Nammāḻvār, his tongue experiences a sweetness comparable to divine nectar. The name of the Ācārya becomes his sustenance, his delight, and his refuge.

tamil_scripts: நாவினால் நவிற்றுஇன்பம் எய்தினேன்மேவினேன்அவன் பொன் அடி மெய்ம்மையேதேவு மற்றறியேன்குருகூர் நம்பிபாவின் இன் இசைபாடித் திரிவனே
english_scripts:
nāvināl naviṭru
inbam eydinēn
mēvinēn
avan pon aḍi meymmaiyē
tēvu maṭraṟiyēn
kurugūr nambi
pāvin in iśai
pāḍi ttirivanē
meaning: My tongue overflowed with bliss as I recited Āḻvār’s pāsurams. I have completely surrendered at his divine feet. I know no refuge apart from this Āḻvār of Thirukkuṟugūr, adorned with all auspicious qualities. With his pāsurams set to music, I shall go everywhere, joyfully singing his glories.
purport:
Madhurakavi Āḻvār continues to sing the glories of Nammāḻvār with unbounded devotion. Such is the greatness of his Ācārya that even without understanding the deeper meanings behind Nammāḻvār's sacred names, merely reciting them fills the heart with an indescribable sweetness. What divine taste lies hidden within those names! Their nectar is not dependent upon intellectual comprehension; it is experienced directly by the devotee whose heart has become attached to the Ācārya.

The feet of Nammāḻvār have completely captivated Madhurakavi Āḻvār. With pure, unwavering, and exclusive devotion, he has surrendered himself entirely unto them. So profound is his attachment that he declares that he knows no other deity apart from Nammāḻvār. This is the highest expression of *Ācārya-bhakti*. For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Nammāḻvār is the one who revealed Bhagavān, instructed him in the truths of the scriptures, and transformed his life. Therefore, his devotion remains firmly fixed upon his Ācārya.

He marvels at the boundless compassion of Nammāḻvār. The mercy of the Ācārya is immediate and tangible, reaching out to uplift even the most fallen jīvātmā. It is this extraordinary compassion that overwhelms Madhurakavi Āḻvār and causes him to celebrate his master in the strongest possible terms. Through Nammāḻvār's grace, he has gained access to the sweetness of Bhagavān and the path leading to eternal service.

Overcome with emotion, he praises the divine pāsurams of Tiruvāymoḻi. To him, these hymns are not merely compositions but an inexhaustible ocean of nectar. Bhagavān, Nammāḻvār, the Tiruvāymoḻi itself, and the musical recitation of its verses merge into a single experience of divine bliss. Every word of Tiruvāymoḻi is saturated with devotion, every verse reveals profound truths, and every melody melts the heart of the listener.

The sweetness of these pāsurams surpasses all other forms of delight. Their musical recitation appears to Madhurakavi Āḻvār even more melodious and nectar-like than the chanting of the Sāma Veda itself. The ears never tire of hearing them, and the heart never becomes satiated with their beauty. The more they are recited, the greater becomes the longing to hear them again.

Therefore, Madhurakavi Āḻvār resolves that he will sing and recite these sacred hymns everywhere. He desires to spend his life celebrating the glory of Nammāḻvār and spreading the nectar of Tiruvāymoḻi throughout the world. His sole refuge, his greatest treasure, and his ultimate goal remain the sacred feet of Teṉkurugūr Nambi.

Thus, he declares his complete surrender to the beneficent Nammāḻvār. Having tasted the sweetness of his Ācārya's names, teachings, and divine hymns, he seeks nothing else. The feet of Nammāḻvār alone are his shelter

tamil_scripts: திரி தந்தாகிலும்தேவ பிரான் உடைகரிய கோலத்திரு உருக் காண்பன் நான்பெரிய வண் குருகூர்நகர் நம்பிக்கு ஆள் உரியனாய்அடியேன்பெற்ற நன்மையே
english_scripts:
tiri tandāgilum\
tēva pirān uḍai\
kariya kōla\
tiru uru kkāṇban nān\
periya vaṇ kurugūr\
nagar nambikkāḻ uriyanāy\
aḍiyēn\
peṭra nanmaiyē
meaning: I, who was once the devoted servitor of Āḻvār, lost hold of that noble position. Yet by his grace, I beheld Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, the dark-hued sovereign of the eternal nityasūrīs. Such wondrous fortune came to me solely because I remained the true servant of the great Āḻvār who incarnated in the generous land of Thirukkuṟugūr.
purport:
By experiencing the pāsurams of Nammāḻvār and witnessing their profound effects, Madhurakavi Āḻvār comes to appreciate the true greatness of his master. It is solely through the grace of Nammāḻvār that he is able to experience Bhagavān Himself. Without the intervention of the Ācārya, the greatness of Bhagavān would have remained inaccessible to him. Therefore, every spiritual experience, every insight, and every glimpse of the Divine is attributed entirely to the compassion and blessings of Nammāḻvār.

Seeing the unparalleled devotion of Madhurakavi Āḻvār towards his Ācārya, Nammāḻvār desired that Bhagavān should reveal Himself to his disciple. Bhagavān, who never allows the wishes of His devotees and Ācāryas to go unfulfilled, gladly accepted this desire. Just as a loving child listens to the words of its mother, Bhagavān listened to Nammāḻvār and manifested Himself before Madhurakavi Āḻvār. Delighted by the extraordinary *Ācārya Śeṣatvam* displayed by Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Bhagavān revealed Himself in His enchanting form as Nīlamegha Śyāma, the dark cloud-hued Lord whose beauty captivates all beings.

Yet, even after receiving this divine vision, Madhurakavi Āḻvār does not attribute it to his own merit. He recognizes that this blessing has come solely through the grace, desire, and intercession of Nammāḻvār. Therefore, while he offers his reverence to Deivapirān, the Lord of the Nityasūris, he does so with the understanding that Bhagavān became accessible to him only because of his Ācārya's compassion. The vision of Bhagavān becomes yet another testimony to the greatness of Nammāḻvār.

Nammāḻvār's heart is filled with immeasurable love for Bhagavān and for Paramapada, the eternal abode where the Nityasūris render uninterrupted service to the Lord. Endowed with countless auspicious qualities and completely absorbed in devotion to Bhagavān, Nammāḻvār stands as the ideal Ācārya. For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, such a master alone is worthy of complete surrender. It is because he surrendered to Nammāḻvār that Bhagavān chose to reveal Himself to him.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār therefore proclaims that he has no desire to approach Bhagavān independently. To seek Bhagavān without the guidance and grace of an Ācārya would be, in his eyes, a grave mistake. The proper path is to approach the Lord through the lineage of Ācāryas, beginning with Nammāḻvār. Only through the mediation of the Ācārya does Bhagavān become truly known, loved, and attained. Thus, he does not adore Bhagavān separately; he adores Bhagavān because Bhagavān is beloved to Nammāḻvār. The Lord becomes precious to him because He is precious to his master.

For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Nammāḻvār remains his refuge, his master, and his everything. The greatness of Bhagavān is not denied, but it is experienced entirely through the lens of Ācārya-bhakti. Even if, due to his own misfortune and accumulated karma, he were somehow to lose the intensity of his devotion towards Nammāḻvār, he declares that he would still remain devoted to Bhagavān, for such devotion itself is a gift received from his Ācārya. The bond established by Nammāḻvār can never truly be broken.

tamil_scripts: நன்மையால் மிக்கநான்மறை ஆளர்கள்புன்மை ஆகக்கருதுவர் ஆதலின்அன்னையாய் அத்தனாய்என்னை ஆண்டிடும் தன்மையான்சடகோபன்என் நம்பியே
english_scripts:
nanmaiyāl mikka\
nānmaṟai āḻargaḻ\
punmai āga\
karuduvar ādalin\
annaiyāy attanāy\
ennai āṇḍiḍum tanmaiyān\
śaḍagōban\
en nambiyē
meaning: Those learned in the four Vedas and renowned for their noble deeds rejected me, considering me lowly and insignificant. But Nammāḻvār accepted me as his own, becoming both my mother and my father. He alone is my refuge, protector, and lord.
purport:
There are great and compassionate personalities who overlook countless faults and focus instead upon a single auspicious quality. Even if a person is burdened with many shortcomings, one noble trait is sufficient for them to shower their grace. Such is their greatness. Just as Gajendra, standing amidst muddy waters, noticed the beauty of a single lotus and desired to offer it to Bhagavān, these exalted beings seek out whatever is good and worthy in others rather than dwelling upon their defects.

There are also those whose compassion extends even towards those who have wronged them. Prahlāda desired forgiveness and welfare for his father Hiraṇyakaśipu, despite the immense suffering inflicted upon him. Sītā Devī, while enduring hardship in Aśokavana, showed kindness towards Trijaṭā and her companions. Similarly, Kūrattāzhvān prayed for the liberation of Nāḷūrān, the very minister whose actions resulted in the loss of his eyesight. Such incidents reveal the extraordinary mercy possessed by the great devotees of Bhagavān.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār, however, speaks from the depths of humility. Although he is adorned with many auspicious qualities, he represents the condition of the ordinary jīvātmā and regards himself as one filled with faults and deficiencies. He feels that even these great and compassionate personalities, who readily overlook the transgressions of others, might reject him because of his innumerable shortcomings.

Yet there is one refuge who never abandons anyone: Nammāḻvār. Madhurakavi Āḻvār proclaims that his Ācārya accepts him without examining whether he possesses virtues or faults. Nammāḻvār's compassion is not dependent upon qualification. He embraces those who seek refuge in him simply because it is his very nature to uplift and protect.

To Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Nammāḻvār fulfills every role necessary for the spiritual welfare of the jīvātmā. Like a mother, he offers unconditional affection and acceptance. Like a father, he imparts instruction and teaches the path of righteousness. Like a leader, he guides the disciple towards Bhagavān and protects him from spiritual downfall. Thus, Nammāḻvār becomes the complete benefactor of the jīvātmā.

The very nature of Śaṭhakōpan is to remove ignorance and destroy everything that obstructs the jīvātmā's progress towards Bhagavān. Therefore, Madhurakavi Āḻvār lovingly addresses him as Śaṭhakōpan. He is also *Nambi*, the perfect and complete one, adorned with every auspicious quality and lacking nothing. For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Nammāḻvār has become everything. He is mother, (father, Ācārya, guide, protector, and master, hence called as nambi.

Having experienced such immeasurable grace, Madhurakavi Āḻvār finds no refuge apart from Nammāḻvār. The one who accepted him without considering his faults, instructed him in the truths of Bhagavān, and led him onto the path of eternal *kainkaryam* has become his all in all. Therefore, he remains firmly established at the sacred feet of Nammāḻvār, whom he regards as his greatest treasure, eternal refuge, and *sarvasvam*.

tamil_scripts: நம்பினேன்பிறர் நன் பொருள் தன்னையும்நம்பினேன்மடவாரையும் முன் எலாம்செம்பொன் மாடத்திருக் குருகூர் நம்பிக்கு அன்பனாய்அடியேன்சதிர்த்தேன் இன்றே
english_scripts:
nambinēn\
piṟar nan poruḻ tannaiyum\
nambinēn\
maḍa vāraiyum mun elām\
śem pon māḍa\
tiru kkurugūr nambikkanbanāy\
aḍiyēn\
śadirttēn inṟē
meaning: In the past, I was attached to worldly pleasures and driven by desire and delusion. Through the grace of Nammāḻvār, I was corrected, uplifted, and transformed into his devoted servitor. That very Nammāḻvār is the illustrious leader of Thirukkuṟugūr, the town adorned with golden mansions.
purport:
Madhurakavi Āḻvār continues to express profound humility while glorifying the transformative grace of Nammāḻvār. He reflects upon his previous condition and how completely his life was redirected by the compassion of his Ācārya. He describes himself as one who had stolen another's property. What property had he stolen, and from whom? The answer lies in the fundamental truth of the relationship between the jīvātmā and Bhagavān.

Every jīvātmā belongs exclusively to Bhagavān. He alone is the rightful owner, while all jīvātmās exist as His eternal servants. Yet, when a person identifies with the notions of "I" and "mine" instead of recognizing their dependence upon Him, they falsely appropriate what belongs to Bhagavān. In that sense, Madhurakavi Āḻvār regards himself as a thief. By forgetting his true nature as a servant and imagining independence, he had unlawfully claimed ownership over what belonged solely to the Lord.

Nor was this his only fault. He had once been attracted to worldly pleasures, material possessions, and sensory enjoyments. Like ordinary people immersed in saṁsāra, his mind wandered towards transient objects and fleeting delights. But that belonged to his past. Everything changed through the grace of Nammāḻvār.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār beautifully compares this transformation to discovering an unexpected treasure. From a distance, he saw a radiant golden lustre shining beyond a great wall. Naturally, he expected to find something valuable, perhaps a heap of precious gems. Yet, when he approached and entered, he discovered something far more valuable than anything he had imagined. He found Nammāḻvār. What are ordinary gems when compared to an Ācārya who reveals Bhagavān and grants the wealth of eternal service? The treasure he discovered surpassed all worldly riches and even exceeded his highest expectations.

Such is the greatness of Nammāḻvār that he was prepared to grant even Vaikuṇṭha itself to Madhurakavi Āḻvār. This raises an astonishing question. How can one who considers himself a thief, burdened with faults and shortcomings, become worthy of such a reward? The answer lies entirely in the boundless compassion of the Ācārya. Nammāḻvār did not scrutinize his defects, nor did he demand qualifications. Instead, he accepted him exactly as he was and resolved to uplift him.

Through his grace, Nammāḻvār transformed Madhurakavi Āḻvār's entire outlook on life. The pride born of ego and possessiveness was removed. In place of self-centredness arose the realization that he was not an independent being but a servant. More specifically, he came to understand himself as a servant of his Ācārya, whose feet became his sole refuge and wealth.

Yet Madhurakavi Āḻvār marvels that Nammāḻvār's grace did not stop there. Accepting him despite all his shortcomings was itself extraordinary. Redirecting his life towards Bhagavān was an even greater blessing. But Nammāḻvār bestowed a favour surpassing all others: he accepted Madhurakavi Āḻvār as his own disciple. He became his Ācārya and took personal responsibility for his spiritual welfare.

For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, this is the pinnacle of grace and compassion. The one who was unworthy was accepted. The one who had forgotten his true nature was instructed. The one who wandered in worldly pursuits was guided towards eternal truth. Therefore, he stands overwhelmed with gratitude, seeing in Nammāḻvār not merely a teacher but the very embodiment of divine mercy, whose compassion transformed a fallen jīvātmā into a devoted servant.

tamil_scripts: இன்று தொட்டும்எழுமையும் எம்பிரான்நின்று தன் புகழ்ஏத்த அருளினான்குன்ற மாடத்திருக் குருகூர் நம்பிஎன்றும் என்னைஇகழ்விலன் காண்மினே
english_scripts:
inṟu toṭṭum\
ezumaiyum embirān\
ninṟu tan pugaz\
ētta aruḻinān\
kunṟa māḍa\
tiru kkurugūr nambi\
enṟum ennai\
igaz vilan kāṇminē
meaning: As the lord of Thirukkuṟugūr, my svāmi Nammāḻvār showered his boundless mercy upon me and inspired me to sing his glories. His compassion is unwavering, and he will never abandon me.
purport:
Immersed in the bliss of his Ācārya's grace, Madhurakavi Āḻvār continues to describe the unique greatness of Nammāḻvār. He reflects upon the distinction between the grace of Bhagavān and the grace of the Ācārya. Once a jīvātmā surrenders at the sacred feet of Nammāḻvār, that relationship continues forever. The disciple remains eternally engaged in the service of the Ācārya, both in this world and in the eternal realm.

Bhagavān, out of His absolute independence (*Svātantrya*), determines when a surrendered jīvātmā will attain Mokṣa and enter Paramapada. The timing rests entirely upon His divine will. The Ācārya's grace, however, manifests immediately and tangibly. From the very moment one takes refuge under the Ācārya, opportunities for service arise. In this material world, one serves the Ācārya through devotion, obedience, and remembrance. Upon attaining Paramapada, that service does not cease, for the relationship with the Ācārya is eternal.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār further reflects upon the accessibility of the Ācārya. Bhagavān is attained through His grace by those who possess the required spiritual maturity, knowledge, devotion, or surrender. The Ācārya, however, extends his compassion even to the most fallen. Nammāḻvār does not wait for qualification. Rather, he himself creates qualification within the disciple. He showers grace even upon those who consider themselves the lowest among the lowly. Such is the boundless mercy of the Ācārya.

Indeed, the devotion shown towards the Ācārya is itself a gift granted by the Ācārya. Left to themselves, jīvātmās wander endlessly in saṁsāra. It is the Ācārya who redirects their lives, implants devotion within their hearts, and teaches them the path leading to Bhagavān. Therefore, the true devotees of the Ācārya cherish service to him above all else. Whether in this world or in Paramapada, their greatest joy lies in serving the one who revealed Bhagavān to them.

Nammāḻvār, the glorious Tirukkurugūr Nambi, is thus celebrated as the embodiment of grace. His compassion does not stand apart from Bhagavān's compassion; rather, it carries and conveys it. Just as a pond contains water drawn from the vast ocean and makes it accessible to those nearby, the Ācārya makes the immeasurable grace of Bhagavān accessible to ordinary jīvātmās.

The greatness of the Ācārya is further demonstrated by Bhagavān Himself. Was it not Bhagavān who appeared as Nara-Nārāyaṇa Ṛṣi and instructed the sacred truths of the Aṣṭākṣarī? Was it not Bhagavān who became the Gītācārya and taught the Bhagavad Gītā to Arjuna? The Lord Himself repeatedly assumes the role of an Ācārya for the upliftment of the world. Such is the exalted nature of the Ācārya's position.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār's praise of Nammāḻvār should not be misunderstood as diminishing the ontological supremacy of Bhagavān. Bhagavān alone remains the Supreme Reality, the ultimate goal, and the master of all. Rather, Madhurakavi Āḻvār is emphasizing the indispensable role of the Ācārya. Without the guidance and grace of the Ācārya, attainment of Bhagavān is impossible. Therefore, he celebrates the greatness of Nammāḻvār with unsurpassed enthusiasm and gratitude.

The grace of the Ācārya is visible and transformative. One can clearly observe the difference between a person before receiving Ācārya-anugraha and after receiving it. The mind becomes purified, conduct becomes refined, devotion becomes steady, and life itself acquires a divine purpose. This transformation is the living testimony to the power of the Ācārya's compassion. Thus, Madhurakavi Āḻvār remains forever immersed in gratitude towards Nammāḻvār, whose grace transformed his life and directed him towards eternal service to Bhagavān.

tamil_scripts: கண்டு கொண்டென்னைக்காரி மாறப்பிரான்பண்டை வல்வினைபாற்றி அருளினான்எண்டிசையும்அறிய இயம்புகேன்ஒண் தமிழ்சடகோபன் அருளையே
english_scripts:
kaṇḍu koṇḍennai\
kāri māṟappirān\
paṇḍai valvinai\
pāṭri aruḻinān\
eṇḍiśaiyum\
aṟiya iyambugēn\
oṇ tamiz\
śaḍagōban aruḻaiyē
meaning: Nammāḻvār, the illustrious son of Poṟkāri and known as Kārimāran, graciously accepted me into his service and erased the sins accumulated from beginningless time. I shall proclaim in all directions the greatness of his mercy and the glory of the divine Tamil pāsurams he composed.
purport:
Nammāḻvār, born to Kari and Uḍaiya Naṅgai, came to be known as Māraṉ and Māri Pirān. Through the divine outpouring of Tiruvāymoḻi, he transformed the direction of devotion for countless jīvātmās and established the path leading directly to Bhagavān. Therefore, Madhurakavi Āḻvār glorifies him as the one who bestows immeasurable benefit upon all, guiding them towards right knowledge and true devotion. In the overwhelming gratitude of Ācārya-bhakti, he regards Nammāḻvār's beneficence as even more immediate and meaningful to him than that of Bhagavān Himself, for it was through Nammāḻvār that Bhagavān became known and attainable.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār especially celebrates the grace-filled glance of his master. Nammāḻvār cast his compassionate eyes upon him and transformed his life forever. The greatness of the Ācārya's glance is beautifully described by Vedānta Deśika in *Subhāṣita Nīvī*: <verse> ekaiva guroḥ dṛṣṭir dvābhyām vāpi labhyate |\
Yan na labhyaṁ aṣṭabhiḥ, sahasreṇāpi kā ratiḥ || </verse>

The meaning conveyed is that a single glance from the Ācārya possesses a salvific power that surpasses even the combined gaze of many divine eyes. Even if one were to combine the three eyes of Śiva, the eight eyes of Brahmā, and the thousand eyes of Indra, they would still not equal the transformative grace contained in a single compassionate glance from an Ācārya directed towards his disciple. The *kaṭākṣa* of the Ācārya is regarded as the supreme means for removing ignorance and bestowing divine grace.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār experiences this truth directly. By the grace of Nammāḻvār's compassionate glance alone, the ignorance accumulated from beginningless time is destroyed. The burden of karma, which had bound him to saṁsāra for countless births, begins to dissolve. Not only are past sins removed, but even those obstacles that hinder service to the Ācārya are gradually eliminated. Such is the power of Nammāḻvār's mercy.

Overwhelmed by gratitude, Madhurakavi Āḻvār resolves to dedicate his life to spreading the glory of his master. Just as messengers travel throughout a village announcing joyful news, he desires to proclaim the greatness of Nammāḻvār in all eight directions of the world. The divine pāsurams of Tiruvāymoḻi are like intoxicating honey, overflowing with sweetness, wisdom, and devotion. Having tasted that nectar himself, he wishes to share it with everyone.

Therefore, he vows to spread the teachings and hymns of Nammāḻvār to the fullest extent of his ability. The one to whom he has surrendered is Śaṭhakōpan, the great saint who overcame the influence of the *śaṭa-vāyu* and remained untouched by the delusions of Māyā. By conquering the forces that bind ordinary jīvātmās to saṁsāra, Nammāḻvār became the beacon who illuminates the path to Bhagavān for all generations.

Thus, Madhurakavi Āḻvār concludes with a heart overflowing with gratitude. The grace-filled glance of Nammāḻvār removed his ignorance, purified his life, and bestowed upon him the wealth of devotion. In return, he seeks only one service: to proclaim the sweetness of Tiruvāymoḻi and the greatness of Śaṭhakōpan throughout the world, so that countless other jīvātmās may likewise come under the shelter of his divine feet.

tamil_scripts: அருள் கொண்டாடும்அடியவர் இன்புறஅருளினான்அவ்வருமறையின் பொருள்அருள் கொண்டுஆயிரம் இன் தமிழ் பாடினான்அருள் கண்டீர்இவ்வுலகினில் மிக்கதே
english_scripts:
aruḻ koṇḍāḍum\
aḍiyavar inbuṟa\
aruḻinān\
avvarumaṟaiyin poruḻ\
aruḻ koṇḍu\
āyiram in tamiz pāḍinān\
aruḻ kaṇḍīr\
ivvulaginil mikkadē
meaning: Out of infinite compassion, Nammāḻvār composed the thousand pāsurams of Thiruvāymoḻi, presenting the very essence of the Vedas for the delight of the Lord’s devotees. This act of grace, through which profound divine truths were made accessible to all, surpasses every other blessing in this world.
purport:
The divine pāsurams of Nammāḻvār are especially relished by those who delight in the glories of Bhagavān. Periyavāccān Piḷḷai, in his commentary, explains that such devotees include the other Āḻvārs themselves, particularly Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār and the great devotees who recognized the immeasurable greatness of Nammāḻvār's compositions. Those whose hearts are immersed in Bhagavān naturally find themselves drawn to Tiruvāymoḻi, for it is nothing less than an ocean of His auspicious qualities, divine sports, and supreme truths.

Through the pāsurams of Tiruvāymoḻi, Nammāḻvār revealed the meanings of the Vedas in a manner accessible to all. The Vedas contain the highest truths concerning Bhagavān, the jīvātmā, and the means to attain Him. Yet their teachings are often presented in concise, symbolic, and deeply encoded language, making them difficult for ordinary people to comprehend. Their true meanings require extensive study, contemplation, and guidance from learned teachers.

Nammāḻvār, however, out of boundless compassion, took those profound truths and expressed them in the sweet language of Tamil. The essential teachings of the Vedas, which remain hidden beneath layers of mantra, upaniṣadic expression, flow openly and beautifully through the verses of Tiruvāymoḻi. What is difficult to grasp in the Vedas becomes clear and accessible through the grace-filled words of Nammāḻvār.

The Vedas themselves declare that their greatness lies in revealing Brahman, Bhagavān. As the scriptures affirm:  brahma̍ṇā̠ vāva sarvē̍ vē̠dā mahī̍yantē

The glory of the Vedas does not arise merely from their antiquity or sacredness, but because they reveal Bhagavān and impart knowledge of His true nature. That knowledge of Bhagavān is the hidden treasure contained within the Vedas. It is their essence, their purpose, and their highest teaching. Nammāḻvār brought forth this hidden treasure and distributed it freely to the world through Tiruvāymoḻi. By the grace bestowed upon him by Bhagavān Himself, he distilled the essence of the Vedas and poured it into the sacred language of Tamil. Therefore, Tiruvāymoḻi is celebrated as the *Drāviḍa Veda*, for it communicates the same eternal truths that are found in the Sanskrit Vedas while making them accessible to all seekers.

For this reason, Madhurakavi Āḻvār regards Nammāḻvār's grace as immeasurable. Bhagavān bestowed His grace upon Nammāḻvār, and Nammāḻvār, in turn, shared that grace with the entire world through his divine compositions. The treasure that remained hidden within the Vedas became available to all through the compassion of the Āḻvār. Periyavāccān Piḷḷai further makes a remarkable observation regarding this pāsuram. He explains that the greatness of Tiruvāymoḻi is not limited to this world alone. Even in Paramapada, the supreme abode of Bhagavān, the divine sweetness of Tiruvāymoḻi is celebrated. Its glory extends beyond the material realm and continues eternally. Such is its excellence that even Bhagavān Himself delights in hearing and enjoying the pāsurams of Nammāḻvār.

Thus, Madhurakavi Āḻvār glorifies Nammāḻvār as the one who unveiled the hidden treasure of the Vedas and offered it to all jīvātmās through Tiruvāymoḻi. The grace that made the inaccessible accessible, the hidden manifest, and the profound understandable is the grace of Nammāḻvār.

tamil_scripts: மிக்க வேதியர்வேதத்தின் உட்பொருள்நிற்கப் பாடிஎன் நெஞ்சுள் நிறுத்தினான்தக்க சீர்ச்சடகோபன் என் நம்பிக்குஆட்புக்க காதல்அடிமைப் பயனன்றே
english_scripts:
mikka vēdiyar\
vēdattin uṭporuḻ\
niṟka ppāḍi\
en neñjuḻ niṟuttinān\
takka śīr\
śaḍagōban en nambikku\
āṭpukka kādal\
aḍimai ppayananṟē
meaning: Nammāḻvār revealed to me the essence of the Vedas, treasured by great scholars, and firmly established that wisdom within my heart. Through his grace, I attained the exalted state of becoming his devoted servitor.
purport:
The Vedas possess immeasurable glory. They reveal truths that cannot be discovered through logic, speculation, or mere intellectual analysis. Bhagavān transcends the grasp of the mind and senses, and therefore knowledge of Him cannot be attained by independent effort alone. Only the Vedas, which originate from Bhagavān Himself, are capable of revealing His true nature, His auspicious qualities, the nature of the jīvātmā, and the means to attain Him. Those who have properly studied, understood, and realized the teachings of the Vedas are indeed worthy of the highest reverence.

Yet even the Vedas remain difficult to comprehend without the grace of an Ācārya. Their teachings are profound and often expressed in subtle and concealed forms. Without proper guidance, the essential meanings remain inaccessible even to the learned. It is only through the compassion of the Ācārya that the hidden truths of the Vedas become clear and capable of being put into practice.

Recognizing the difficulty faced by ordinary people, Nammāḻvār out of boundless compassion composed the Tiruvāymoḻi. The profound teachings that are scattered throughout the Vedas were gathered together and presented in sweet Tamil verses so that they could remain firmly established in the minds of devotees. What is difficult to grasp in the Vedas becomes natural and accessible through the pāsurams of Tiruvāymoḻi. Nammāḻvār not only explained the truths of the Vedas but also enabled devotees to internalize them and live according to them.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār, representing the condition of ordinary jīvātmās, marvels at this grace. He describes his own mind as being hard like stone, incapable of understanding lofty spiritual truths. Yet the pāsurams of Nammāḻvār penetrated even such a hardened mind and revealed the treasures hidden within the Vedas. Through Tiruvāymoḻi, he came to understand the true nature of the jīvātmā and its eternal relationship with Bhagavān. More importantly, these pāsurams immersed his mind in *Bhagavat-śeṣatvam*, the realization that the jīvātmā exists solely for the service and pleasure of Bhagavān.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār therefore declares that Śaṭhakōpan alone is truly qualified to sing the glories of Bhagavān. Who else possesses such purity of heart, such realization of divine truths, and such intimate experience of Bhagavān's auspicious qualities? Nammāḻvār alone was uniquely fitted for this sacred task. Through Tiruvāymoḻi, he revealed Bhagavān in a manner that no one else could. Yet what amazes Madhurakavi Āḻvār even more is Nammāḻvār's compassion. The very Āḻvār who was qualified to glorify Bhagavān in the highest manner did not remain distant and inaccessible. Instead, he accepted even an insignificant person such as Madhurakavi Āḻvār. Therefore, Nammāḻvār is not merely Śaṭhakōpan, the revealer of divine truths, but also Nambi, the complete and compassionate master who graciously accepted an unworthy disciple.

The greatest wonder, according to Madhurakavi Āḻvār, is the immediate efficacy of the Ācārya's grace. The moment a genuine desire arises to serve the Ācārya, the Ācārya responds with compassion and acceptance. Through his grace, the disciple is led towards surrender (*śaraṇāgati*) and spiritual transformation. The path that would otherwise require immense effort and countless qualifications becomes attainable through the mercy of the Ācārya.

Thus, Madhurakavi Āḻvār concludes that Nammāḻvār's compassion is unparalleled. The one who revealed the essence of the Vedas, established countless jīvātmās in Bhagavat-śeṣatvam, and accepted even the most unworthy among them as his own disciple remains his sole refuge. Therefore, he clings firmly to the feet of Nammāḻvār, convinced that the grace of the Ācārya is the surest means to attain Bhagavān and eternal service at His divine feet.

payan anṟāgilum\
pāṅgallar āgilum\
śeyal nanṟāga\
tirutti ppaṇi koḻvān\

kurugūr nambi\
muyalginṟēn\
un tan moy kazaṟkanbaiyē
meaning: O Nammāḻvār, who dwells in fertile Thirukkuṟugūr where cuckoos sing amidst flourishing groves! Though you seek no personal gain, you tirelessly uplift the people of the world, guiding them toward divine servitude through your words and example. It is toward such a compassionate master that I continually deepen my affection.
purport:
In this pāsuram, Madhurakavi Āḻvār provides a clear and concise instruction regarding the indispensable role of the Ācārya. It is the Ācārya alone who makes a jīvātmā realize its true nature. Without the grace of the Ācārya, how can one understand that one's real identity is not that of an independent being, but that of a servant of the servants of Bhagavān? *Bhāgavata-śeṣatvam* is the true svarūpa of the jīvātmā, while *Bhagavat-śeṣatvam* is its eternal and intrinsic nature. These truths, though repeatedly taught in the scriptures, become firmly established in the heart only through the compassionate guidance of the Ācārya.

The greatness of the Ācārya lies in the fact that he seeks nothing in return for this service. He gains no personal benefit by correcting, instructing, and uplifting others. His actions are motivated solely by compassion. Throughout the scriptures we find numerous examples of exalted personalities who instructed others without any selfish motive. Sītā Devī advised Rāvaṇa to abandon his sinful desire and return to the path of righteousness. Vibhīṣaṇa repeatedly counselled Rāvaṇa to release Sītā and avoid enmity with Śrī Rāma. Prahlāda instructed his father Hiraṇyakaśipu that Nārāyaṇa alone is the true protector, father, and master of all beings. None of them stood to gain personally from offering such advice. They spoke only out of compassion and a desire for the welfare of others.

The Āḻvārs and Ācāryas stand in the same tradition. They derive no benefit by correcting us, teaching us the truths of the scriptures, or directing us towards Bhagavān. Their sole purpose is the upliftment of jīvātmās. Even when faced with individuals who seem unwilling to change, like Rāvaṇa or Hiraṇyakaśipu, compassionate teachers continue to show the proper path and impart right knowledge. Whether the disciple is receptive or resistant, qualified or unqualified, the Ācārya never abandons his duty. He continues to bestow grace and guidance without discrimination.

Such is Nammāḻvār, the embodiment of all auspicious qualities. Born in sacred Tirukkurugūr, he appeared for the welfare of all jīvātmās. The holy land of Tirukkurugūr itself is celebrated for its beauty, where nature joins in devotion to Bhagavān. The birds, trees, rivers, and all living beings seem to participate in the divine atmosphere created by Nammāḻvār's presence and his songs glorifying Bhagavān. Through the pāsurams of Tiruvāymoḻi, he repeatedly called out to Bhagavān with intense longing, inviting Him to manifest for the benefit of devotees.

It is this Nammāḻvār who became the Ācārya of Madhurakavi Āḻvār. Reflecting upon the immeasurable compassion and greatness of his master, Madhurakavi Āḻvār desires only one thing: that his devotion towards the sacred lotus feet of Nammāḻvār should continue to grow without limit. He seeks neither worldly prosperity nor even the joys of heaven. His sole aspiration is to deepen his attachment to the Ācārya who revealed his true nature, corrected his misconceptions, and established him firmly in the path of eternal service to Bhagavān.

anban tannai\
aḍaindavargaṭkellām anban\
ten kurugūr\
nagar nambikku\
anbanāy\
madurakavi śonna śol nambuvār padi\
vaigundam kāṇminē
meaning: Emperumān lovingly embraces all beings, especially His devoted servants. Nammāḻvār, in turn, cherishes those very devotees of the Lord. I, Madhurakavi Āḻvār, remain steadfast in my affection for Nammāḻvār. Those who recite these verses with devotion will attain the radiant abode of Śrī Vaikuṇṭham and dwell there eternally.
purport:
In the final pāsuram of *Kaṇṇinuṇ Ciṟuttāmbu*, Madhurakavi Āḻvār brings his Prabandham to a glorious conclusion by summarizing the entire philosophy of Ācārya-bhakti. Throughout these eleven pāsurams, he has demonstrated that Nammāḻvār is his sole refuge, master, and means to attain Bhagavān. In this concluding verse, he extends that blessing to all who follow the same path.

The pāsuram reveals a beautiful hierarchy of devotion. At the highest level stands Bhagavān, the loving Lord (*Anban*), who is dear to all devotees and who showers His grace upon the universe. Nammāḻvār stands as the foremost devotee of Bhagavān and the embodiment of *Bhāgavata-bhakti*. Having attained the Lord and become immersed in His service, he serves as the perfect guide for all jīvātmās. Madhurakavi Āḻvār then stands as the ideal disciple, demonstrating unwavering devotion towards his Ācārya. Finally come those devotees who place their trust in the teachings of Madhurakavi Āḻvār and walk the path shown by him. Thus, the flow of grace descends through the lineage of devotion, from Bhagavān to Nammāḻvār, from Nammāḻvār to Madhurakavi Āḻvār, and from Madhurakavi Āḻvār to all future devotees.

The central message of the pāsuram is that those who faithfully accept the teachings of Madhurakavi Āḻvār and cultivate devotion towards Nammāḻvār will surely attain the highest spiritual goal. The path of the Ācārya is presented not merely as one among many means, but as the most secure and compassionate route to Bhagavān.

Madhurakavi Āḻvār concludes by inviting devotees to behold *Vaikuṇṭha* through the famous expression *"Vaikuṇṭham Kaṇmiṉē."* This statement carries several layers of meaning. At one level, it refers to the eternal abode of Bhagavān, Paramapada, which is the destination of liberated jīvātmās. At another level, it teaches that wherever a true Ācārya resides, that place itself becomes comparable to Vaikuṇṭha, for it is there that divine knowledge, devotion, and grace are freely distributed. The presence of an Ācārya transforms the ordinary into the sacred.

The commentators further explain that *Vaikuṇṭham Kaṇmiṉē* points towards the ultimate attainment of the jīvātmā. After completing its journey through saṁsāra, the liberated jīvātmā reaches Paramapada and continues rendering eternal *kainkaryam*. For Madhurakavi Āḻvār, this eternal service is inseparable from service to the Ācārya, for the relationship established with the Ācārya does not cease upon liberation but continues forever.

Periyavāccān Piḷḷai offers a particularly beautiful interpretation. He explains that while Āḻvār Tirunagari in this world is shared by Bhagavān and Nammāḻvār, Paramapada may be viewed as the realm where Nammāḻvār's greatness shines forth most brilliantly. Therefore, for those who have taken refuge in Nammāḻvār through Madhurakavi Āḻvār, Vaikuṇṭha becomes especially desirable because it is there that they may eternally remain in the company of their Ācārya and continue serving him without interruption.

The relationship between Bhagavān, Ācārya, and disciple may be understood through a simple analogy. Bhagavān is the source of all grace, like the source of electrical power. Nammāḻvār is connected directly to that source, while Madhurakavi Āḻvār remains firmly connected to Nammāḻvār. Those who hold on to Madhurakavi Āḻvār likewise become connected to that uninterrupted current of divine grace. One need not attempt to reach the source independently; by remaining attached to the lineage, the grace naturally flows.

This teaching beautifully echoes the words of Swāmi Vedānta Deśika, who praises the *tol vazhi*, the ancient and time-honoured path of the Ācāryas. The surest means of attaining Bhagavān is not self-reliance, scholarship, austerity, or personal effort alone, but humble dependence upon the grace of the Ācārya. Through the Ācārya, the meanings of the scriptures become clear. Through the Ācārya, devotion becomes firm. Through the Ācārya, surrender becomes possible. Through the Ācārya, Bhagavān becomes attainable.

Thus, Madhurakavi Āḻvār concludes *Kaṇṇinuṇ Ciṟuttāmbu* by glorifying the path of Ācārya-bhakti. The one who accepts Nammāḻvār as his refuge, follows the teachings transmitted through Madhurakavi Āḻvār, and remains steadfast in service to the Ācārya will surely attain the highest goal. Such a devotee will behold Vaikuṇṭha, enjoy the company of Bhagavān, the Nityasūris, and the Ācāryas, and engage forever in uninterrupted *kainkaryam*. This is the supreme blessing that Madhurakavi Āḻvār bestows upon all who study and cherish this divine Prabandham.
